crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Collecting Emissions Data
children.blurb: Collecting emissions data covers the activity data and calculated totals for greenhouse gases across an organisation's operations and value chain.

children.name: Checking Claims Against the Ledger
children.blurb: Checking claims against the ledger means comparing a sustainability or carbon claim with the accounting records that support it.

children.name: Combining Financial and Non-Financial Data
children.blurb: Combining financial and non-financial data in sustainability and carbon accounting means linking monetary figures from the general ledger, such as operating costs, capital expenditure, and revenue, with physical and social measures like greenhouse gas emissions, energy use, water withdrawal, and workforce metrics.

children.name: Drafting Sustainability Disclosures
children.blurb: Drafting sustainability disclosures covers the narrative and numerical parts of corporate reports on climate, emissions, workforce, community, governance, and supply chain matters.

children.name: Carbon Credit Records
children.blurb: Carbon credit records are the structured data that track the lifecycle of a carbon credit, from issuance through ownership changes to retirement.

sections.body: AI in sustainability and carbon accounting is mostly doing document work at scale. It reads utility bills, fuel receipts, shipping manifests, meter exports, invoices, and supplier spreadsheets, then pulls out activity data and converts it into emissions estimates. It classifies spend into categories, flags missing fields, and reconciles figures across systems that were never designed to talk to each other. It also checks public claims against internal ledgers and drafts first versions of disclosure text. The work is practical and repetitive, which is why it has moved faster than many strategic climate projects.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The settled part is extraction, classification, and anomaly detection on structured and semi-structured records. Models can find a meter reading in a PDF, match an invoice to a purchase order, and highlight a number that moved without explanation. The unsettled part is assurance. Scope 3 data depends on suppliers who report late, use different methods, or estimate rather than measure, and AI cannot turn that into verified fact. Carbon credit records add another layer because registry data, retirement claims, and double counting checks require careful human judgment and legal review. The site's 222 compliance and regulation pages reflect how much of this field is governed by disclosure rules, not by model accuracy alone. AI can speed up preparation, but it cannot sign off an audit, resolve a methodological dispute, or guarantee that a claim will survive regulatory scrutiny.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages here follow the accounting chain from raw data to public claim. Collecting Emissions Data is the entry point for meter readings, invoices, travel records, and supplier files, and it covers how those inputs are captured and standardized. Checking Claims Against the Ledger is where a stated emissions figure or green claim is tested against the underlying records, which is the control step that auditors and regulators care about. Combining Financial and Non-Financial Data explains how carbon numbers sit beside revenue, cost, and asset data in one reporting model, which is the bridge to mainstream accounting. Drafting Sustainability Disclosures takes the reconciled numbers and turns them into narrative and tabular disclosure text, with review points for legal and assurance teams. Carbon Credit Records is the specialist page for offsets, retirements, registry entries, and the traceability problems that make credits a separate accounting challenge.
